payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Are both the mug and the headphones visible enough to compare their positions?
node.criteria: Pass if the mug and headphones are identifiable and their relative positions can be judged; fail if the image clearly shows either is absent or the comparison is impossible; unknown if visibility or identification is inconclusive.
node.binding: Use only the image to identify the mug and headphones and assess whether their relative placement is observable. This establishes evidence availability, not fulfillment.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image clearly shows a mug and headphones, and their relative positions are observable: the mug is to the right of the headphones. Both objects are identifiable enough for comparison.

fulfillment: The binding is too broad and the node treats the final spatial relation as sufficient proof of the requested edit. In the edited image, a mug is indeed to the right of the headphones, but the source shows the mug to their left; the edit appears to add/move a mug to the right while leaving a mug-like object on the left, so the requested change has progressed without clearly being completed. Make the criterion compare the same target mug’s position in the source and edited snapshots, and distinguish partial progress from completion when the requested relocation is not unambiguously complete. Do not infer completion from two support observations that repeat the same final-state claim; they are dependent on the same evidence, not independent confirmation. Preserve unknown for genuinely insufficient evidence, and keep transport/schema failures separate from visual evidence—none are reported here.
s2: The binding checks only whether a mug is right of the headphones in the edited snapshot, so it mistakes a final-state relation for completion of the requested relocation. Make the node track the same source mug across snapshots and assess its displacement relative to the headphones; distinguish a completed move from partial progress when the original mug remains or the target’s identity/continuity is ambiguous. Here the source mug is left of the headphones, while the edited image appears to retain a mug on the left and show another on the right, supporting progress but not clearly proving the original mug was moved. Avoid treating the dependent s1/s2 observations as independent confirmation. Keep unknown for genuinely unresolved identity or visibility, and do not conflate visual uncertainty with transport/schema failure (none is reported).
